title: The Flight of Bees: Nature's Most Delicate Collaboration
title_zh: 蜜蜂的飞行：自然界最精巧的协作
intro_zh: 本文约900词，实际目标词数约900词，新词6个，难度适中。内容讲述蜜蜂授粉的机制、生态价值与面临的挑战。

paragraphs.en: Every spring, when flowers begin to bloom, a quiet but vital process takes place all around us. Bees, those tiny buzzing creatures, are not just making honey — they are performing an essential service for the natural world. Pollinate is the act of transferring pollen from the male part of a flower to the female part, enabling fertilization and the production of seeds and fruits. Without bees, many of the foods we enjoy would simply disappear.
paragraphs.zh: 每年春天，当花朵开始绽放时，一个安静但至关重要的过程就在我们身边发生。蜜蜂，这些嗡嗡作响的小生物，不仅仅是在酿蜜——它们还在为自然界提供一种必不可少的服务。授粉是将花粉从花的雄性部分传到雌性部分的行为，从而促进受精并产生种子和果实。没有蜜蜂，我们享用的许多食物就会消失。

paragraphs.en: The process of pollination is a wonderful example of cooperation. When a bee lands on a flower, it is usually looking for nectar, a sweet liquid that provides energy for the bee. As the bee pushes its head deep into the flower to drink the nectar, its body brushes against the pollen-producing parts. The yellow dust, known as pollen, sticks to the bee's hairy body. When the bee then flies to the next flower, some of this pollen rubs off onto the female part of that flower, completing the pollination.
paragraphs.zh: 授粉过程是合作的一个绝妙例证。当蜜蜂落在一朵花上时，它通常是在寻找花蜜，一种为蜜蜂提供能量的甜味液体。当蜜蜂将头部深深探入花朵吸食花蜜时，它的身体会擦过产生花粉的部分。被称为花粉的黄色粉尘会粘在蜜蜂毛茸茸的身体上。当蜜蜂随后飞到下一朵花时，其中一些花粉就会蹭到那朵花的雌性部分，从而完成授粉。

paragraphs.en: Bees have evolved with remarkable skill for this task. Their bodies are covered with fine hairs that act like tiny brushes, making it easy for pollen to attach. Some bees even have special structures called pollen baskets on their hind legs. Unlike other insects, bees deliberately collect pollen, mixing it with a little nectar to form a sticky ball that they carry back to their colony. This purposeful behavior makes them far more efficient pollinators than butterflies, birds or beetles.
paragraphs.zh: 蜜蜂进化出了非凡的能力来完成这项任务。它们的身体覆盖着细小的绒毛，就像微型刷子，使花粉很容易附着。有些蜜蜂甚至在后腿上有叫做花粉筐的特殊结构。与其他昆虫不同，蜜蜂会刻意收集花粉，将花粉与少量花蜜混合成黏性小球，带回它们的蜂群。这种有目的的行为使它们比蝴蝶、鸟类或甲虫高效得多。

paragraphs.en: The numbers are astonishing. Scientists estimate that bees are responsible for pollinating about 75-85% of the world's flowering plant species. In agriculture, honeybees alone contribute to the production of more than 90 commercial crops, including apples, almonds, blueberries and tomatoes. The global economic value of insect pollination is estimated at over 235 billion US dollars per year. In China, where many fruit orchards depend on bees, the loss of these pollinators would cause a severe drop in fruit yields and a sharp rise in food prices.
paragraphs.zh: 这些数字令人惊叹。科学家估计，世界上大约75%至85%的开花植物物种都依赖蜜蜂授粉。在农业中，仅蜜蜂就为90多种商业作物做出了贡献，包括苹果、杏仁、蓝莓和西红柿。昆虫授粉的全球经济价值估计每年超过2350亿美元。在中国，许多果园依赖蜜蜂，这些传粉者的丧失将导致水果产量急剧下降和食品价格大幅上涨。

paragraphs.en: Take the almond as a concrete example. In California, which produces more than 80% of the world's almonds, every spring beekeepers transport millions of hives to almond orchards. The trees rely almost entirely on bees for pollination; without them, an almond blossom would never become an almond. This shows how a single ecosystem relies on the delicate balance between animal and plant. Even tiny changes in bee populations can lead to huge effects on our plates.
paragraphs.zh: 以杏仁为具体例子。在加利福尼亚，该地生产世界80%以上的杏仁，每年春天蜂农会将数百万个蜂箱运到杏仁果园。杏仁树几乎完全依赖蜜蜂授粉；没有蜜蜂，一朵杏花永远不会变成杏仁。这表明一个生态系统如何依赖于动植物之间的微妙平衡。即使是蜜蜂种群数量的微小变化，也会对我们的餐桌产生巨大影响。

paragraphs.en: However, bees are in trouble. Over the past few decades, beekeepers around the world have reported a worrying phenomenon called colony collapse disorder, where worker bees suddenly disappear from a hive, leaving the queen and young bees to die. The causes are complex but include the use of pesticide, loss of wildflower habitats, climate change, and mites that attack bee colonies. In China, intensive farming and urban expansion have also reduced the places where bees can find food and shelter.
paragraphs.zh: 然而，蜜蜂正陷入困境。在过去的几十年里，世界各地的养蜂人报告了一种令人担忧的现象，称为蜂群崩溃综合症，工蜂突然从蜂巢中消失，留下蜂王和幼蜂面临死亡。原因很复杂，但包括使用杀虫剂、野花栖息地丧失、气候变化，以及攻击蜂群的螨虫。在中国，集约农业和城市扩张也减少了蜜蜂寻找食物和庇护所的场所。

paragraphs.en: The loss of bees would be a disaster not only for agriculture but for the whole natural world. Many wild plants rely on bees to reproduce, and the animals that eat those plants would also suffer. For example, if bees disappeared, the seeds of many wildflowers would not form, and the insects that feed on them would starve, leading to a collapse of entire food chains. This ripple effect reminds us that every species, no matter how small, has a role in the web of life.
paragraphs.zh: 蜜蜂的消失不仅是农业的灾难，也是整个自然界的灾难。许多野生植物依赖蜜蜂繁殖，而食用这些植物的动物也会受到影响。例如，如果蜜蜂消失，许多野花的种子就无法形成，以它们为食的昆虫会饿死，导致整个食物链崩溃。这种连锁效应提醒我们，每一个物种，无论多么微小，都在生命之网中扮演一个角色。

paragraphs.en: But there is hope. People around the world are taking action to protect bees. Some farmers are reducing the use of pesticides and planting strips of wildflowers along the edges of fields. City dwellers are creating rooftop gardens and balcony planters with bee-friendly plants. Scientists are breeding bees that are more resistant to disease. In China, the government has placed increasing importance on ecological protection. Every one of us can help by planting a flower or avoiding garden chemicals. A small effort can make a big difference for our buzzing little friends.
paragraphs.zh: 但仍有希望。世界各地的人们正在采取行动保护蜜蜂。一些农民正在减少使用杀虫剂，并在田边种植野花带。城市居民正在创建屋顶花园和阳台种植箱，种植对蜜蜂友好的植物。科学家正在培育更能抵抗疾病的蜜蜂种群。在中国，政府越来越重视生态保护。我们每个人都可以通过种植一朵花或避免使用园艺化学品来提供帮助。小小的努力可以为我们嗡嗡作响的小朋友带来巨大的改变。

questions.q: What is the main purpose of this article?
options: A. To explain how bees make honey
B. To describe the importance of bee pollination and the dangers bees face
C. To compare different types of pollinators
D. To show how to keep bees as pets
questions.explain: 主旨题。文章首先说明蜜蜂授粉的重要性，然后详细介绍授粉过程、经济价值、面临的威胁以及保护措施。因此主要目的是描述蜜蜂授粉的重要性及其面临的危险。选项A只提到酿蜜，C和D不是文章重点。

questions.q: According to the article, which of the following is NOT a reason for the decline of bees?
options: C. The increasing number of bee colonies
questions.explain: 细节题。第六段列举了蜜蜂减少的原因，包括杀虫剂、栖息地丧失、气候变化和螨虫。选项C（蜂群数量增加）不是原因，因此是正确答案。

questions.q: What can be inferred about the relationship between bees and almond trees?
options: A. Almond trees do not need bees for fertilization
B. Bees only produce honey from almond flowers
C. Almond trees rely almost entirely on bees for pollination
D. Without bees, almond trees would still produce as many almonds
questions.explain: 推断题。第五段明确指出杏仁树几乎完全依赖蜜蜂授粉；没有蜜蜂，杏花永远不会变成杏仁。因此推断为C。A和D与文意相反，B在文中未提及。

questions.q: The word 'pollinate' in the first paragraph probably means ______.
options: A. to make honey from flowers
B. to transfer pollen to enable fertilization
C. to collect nectar from flowers
D. to protect flowers from insects
questions.explain: 词义题。第一段中“Pollinate”后的解释是“transferring pollen from the male part of a flower to the female part, enabling fertilization”，即传递花粉以完成受精。所以选B。
